answers.transcript:
Okay, I will talk about a gift what I gave to my sister last year.
It was her birthday, she become twenty-five years old.
I thinked a lot about the present for two weeks because she is very difficult person.
At the end I buyed a camera, not a professional one, a small old style camera.
She likes to take photos of the street and the cats, she puts them in Instagram.
I chose this camera because her old one broke during our holiday in Antalya two years ago.
When she opened the box in the kitchen she was very very surprised and she screamed.
She hugged me and she said thank you many times, my mother also was crying.
After that day she take photos of everything, even the food in the table.
I am very happy because for her it was a really good surprise, and she uses it also today.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The order gift, person, reason and reaction is proper and the talk does not break off, but the reaction section ends in two sentences. Links are limited to "At the end", "After that day", "because", and sentences proceed at the same length.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Vocabulary describing the choice of gift is next to none: present, gift, camera, photos, surprised repeat. "Old style camera" is the right idea but does not land in the right form (vintage / second hand does not come up).
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Form errors in irregular verbs (thinked, buyed, she become), a relative pronoun (a gift what), prepositions (in Instagram, in the table) and agreement (she take) are in most sentences. Structures are simple; there is no complex structure beyond the when and because clauses.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Tell the sister's reaction as a scene — what she said, what she did — because at present it is skimmed with "she screamed" and "she hugged me". In the language, first fix the irregular verbs (thought / bought), since all three sit at the narrative's turning point.

answers.transcript:
So the gift I want to talk about is a camera which I gave to my sister for her twenty-fifth birthday last year.
She is a person who is really difficult to buy something for, so I was thinking about it for maybe two weeks.
In the end I decided a camera, because her old one was broken during a holiday and after that she never replaced it.
It wasn't an expensive professional one, it was a small vintage camera, second hand actually, and I found it in a shop in the old bazaar.
She takes photos all the time, mostly of street cats and old doors, and she shares them in Instagram.
So I thought it was something that she would really use, not a present that stays in the cupboard for years.
When she opened it, first she didn't say nothing for two seconds, and after that she started to shout.
My mother was crying also, which was a little bit exaggerated in my opinion.
For one month she was taking photos of everything, even our dinner table, and my father was complaining about this.
So I can say that it went down well, and honestly it was a big relief for me.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: All four points are developed and the link between the reason for the choice and the reaction is built. The flow becomes mechanical: sections open in the same pattern with "So", "In the end", "When she opened it", "So I can say", and the detail about the mother slows the narrative by one sentence.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is vocabulary to describe the choice of gift (second hand, vintage camera, went down well, relief), and meaning is clear throughout. The choice slips in two places: "she shares them in Instagram", and no more natural pattern comes up in place of "she would really use".
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: A relative clause, the past continuous and that-clauses are controlled, and more than two-thirds of sentences are error-free. The remaining errors sit in a narrow set: verb pattern (I decided a camera), preposition (in Instagram), a double negative (she didn't say nothing).

answers.what_would_lift_it: Run the reason for choosing the camera for this person one sentence further: "difficult to buy for" is a good start but is not backed with an example. In the language, fix the pattern "decide on something" and the negation "didn't say anything".

answers.transcript:
Okay, so the gift I've chosen is a camera I bought my sister for her twenty-fifth, which was, what, about a year ago now.
She's notoriously impossible to buy for. She never wants anything, and if she does want something she's usually gone and bought it herself already, so I racked my brains for a good couple of weeks.
What I landed on was an old film camera, a second-hand one from a little shop in the bazaar. Nothing fancy, and definitely not the sort of thing she'd have picked out herself.
The reason I went for it was that she's always photographing things, street cats, old doors, that kind of thing, but she does it all on her phone, and she'd been going on for ages about how film looks different.
So it was a bit of a gamble, but at least it was something she'd actually use rather than something that ends up at the back of a cupboard.
And she loved it. She went completely silent for a second, which from her is saying something, and then she was straight out on the balcony taking pictures of the neighbour's washing.
It went down really well. She still uses it, which is the part I'm most pleased about, because most presents get put away after a fortnight and that's the last you see of them.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The narrative is fluent and the reaction section ties to a single scene (pulling the neighbour's washing line on the balcony). There is one self-correction ("which was, what, about a year ago now"), the rare kind of pause that eight lines allow.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items are plentiful and correctly placed: notoriously impossible to buy for, racked my brains, what I landed on, nothing fancy, going on for ages, a bit of a gamble, at the back of a cupboard, went down really well, that's the last you see of them.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Structural range is wide: the past perfect continuous (she'd been going on), an emphatic conditional with "if she does want something", relative clauses, "she'd have picked out herself". Errors are rare; "she's usually gone and bought it herself already" is natural in speech and costs the listener nothing.

answers.what_would_lift_it: This is on target; for the next level up, the idea "a bit of a gamble" needs to be called back in the closing — saying why the risk paid off. There is nothing left to do in the language.
